teacup.title: 茶壶
teacup.description: 青色茶壶的釉彩技艺起源于宋代龙泉窑,与东青釉同源发展。明代正德年间,釉色浅淡闪黄;至清代景德镇仿制时称"嫩龙泉釉",康熙时期烧制出釉质坚硬、色泽深润的豆青釉。清代豆青色进一步趋近绿色,成为独立釉色体系。豆青釉的烧制工艺复杂,需在高温下控制釉色变化,形成独特的色泽和质感。Green teapot glaze technology originated in the Song Dynasty Longquan kilns, and the development of the same source of the East Green glaze. During the Zhengde period of the Ming dynasty, the glaze color was light and flashing yellow; to the Qing dynasty Jingdezhen imitation called "tender Longquan glaze", the Kangxi period fired a hard glaze, color and lustre of the dark soybean green glaze. Qing dynasty bean green color further tends to green, become an independent glaze color system. Bean green glaze firing process is complex, need to control the glaze color changes at high temperatures to form a unique color and texture.

modelNew.title: 乐舞俑
modelNew.description: 乐舞俑是中国古代用于殉葬的陶俑,主要表现乐舞表演场景,反映了古代社会的音乐、舞蹈文化及丧葬习俗。唐代乐舞俑尤为突出,常见三彩釉陶工艺,题材包括宫廷乐舞、胡人表演等,现多收藏于陕西历史博物馆、中国国家博物馆等机构。Terracotta figurines of music and dance were used for burial in ancient China, mainly showing the scenes of music and dance performances, reflecting the music, dance culture and funeral customs of ancient society. The Tang Dynasty terracotta figurines of music and dance are especially prominent, and are commonly made of three-color glazed pottery, with themes including court music and dance and hu-man performances, etc. They are now mostly collected in the Shaanxi Museum of History, the National Museum of China, and other institutions.

copper-chew.title: 二里头文化青铜器
copper-chew.description: 二里头文化青铜器以中国河南省洛阳市偃师二里头遗址命名的同类型文化遗存出土的青铜器。年代约当公元前21～前16世纪。可分为 4期,青铜器大部分属于第三期。二里头文化青铜器的年代,有夏代晚期和商代早期两种不同看法。在这个遗址的晚期堆积中,曾发现过一些小件青铜器。1973年第一次在第三期堆积层中出土了一件青铜容器爵,以后又陆续有所发现。Erlitou Culture Bronzes Bronzes excavated from the remains of the same type of culture named after the Erlitou site in Yanshi, Luoyang City, Henan Province, China. The date is about 21st to 16th century BC. Can be divided into 4 phases, most of the bronzes belong to the third phase. There are two different views on the age of the Erlitou culture bronzes, the late Xia Dynasty and the early Shang Dynasty. In the late accumulation of this site, there have been found some small pieces of bronze. 1973 in the third phase of the accumulation layer for the first time in the unearthed a bronze container jue, and later found one after another.

armillary_sphere_1771.title: 浑天仪
armillary_sphere_1771.description: 此次展出的展品是一件天文仪器，一个天球模型。它用于演示天象，并确定时间、赤道坐标和黄道坐标。浑天仪能够模拟各种天文现象，包括行星相对于太阳的运动。它由弗朗西斯谢克·斯武普斯基（Franciszek Słupski）制作，是他在克拉科夫大学哲学系博士论文的一部分。浑天仪由同心圆环组成，代表天球的大圆。地平环固定在一个木质底座上，底座由两个交叉的雕花木臂组成，木臂安装在一个异形底座上，底座中央放置一个罗盘。小时环垂直于地平环固定，内藏一个由约翰内斯·弗赖特霍夫（Johannes Vrijthoff）在南极制造的时钟装置。该装置通过用小球设置内部的大圆和轴来驱动浑天仪。The exhibit on display is an astronomical instrument, a celestial sphere model. It is used to demonstrate celestial phenomena and to determine time, equatorial coordinates, and ecliptic coordinates. The armillary sphere can simulate various astronomical phenomena, including the motion of planets relative to the sun. It was made by Franciszek Słupski as part of his doctoral dissertation in the Faculty of Philosophy at the University of Krakow. The armillary sphere consists of concentric rings representing the great circles of the celestial sphere. The horizon ring is fixed to a wooden base composed of two crossed, carved wooden arms mounted on a shaped base with a compass in the center. The hour ring is fixed perpendicular to the horizon ring and contains a clock mechanism made by Johannes Vrijthoff at the South Pole. The device drives the armillary sphere by setting the inner great circles and axes with small balls.

ding_censer_with_an_openwork_cover.title: 鼎式镂空盖香炉
ding_censer_with_an_openwork_cover.description: 这件香炉采用掐丝珐琅工艺装饰，与镀金金属片的图形和镂空装饰完美契合——掐丝珐琅隔层的金属丝和边缘凸显了植物藤蔓的图案。这件色彩丰富的装饰以龙及其丰富的造型为主导图案。This censer is decorated with cloisonné enamel, which perfectly matches the graphics and openwork decoration of the gilded metal sheets—the wires and edges of the cloisonné compartments highlight the pattern of plant vines. This richly colored decoration is dominated by the motif of the dragon and its rich forms.

mass_chalice.title: 弥撒圣杯
mass_chalice.description: 这里展示的圣杯由圣墓骑士团成员约瑟夫·马约维奇神父于1773年捐赠给梅胡夫的圣十字医院教堂。该圣杯由马钦·莱克斯奇基（Marcin Lekszycki）制作，他于1763年至1798年在克拉科夫担任金匠，是当时的一位金匠大师。他是克拉科夫少数几位在作品上署名的金匠之一（使用椭圆形内的“ML”行会标志）。莱克斯奇基经营着一家大型作坊，拥有众多学徒；他的作坊位于布拉卡街（Bracka Street）。他创作了独特的洛可可风格的圣体匣、圣体盒、圣杯、长明灯、香炉、香舟、托盘和烛台。马钦·莱克斯奇作坊的大部分作品都收藏于克拉科夫和前梅胡夫区的教堂中。这里展示的圣杯由镀金银制成。它采用洛可可风格（贝壳）装饰，并具有莱克斯奇基工作室典型的装饰元素，如藤蔓、花彩、莨苕叶和植物图案。The chalice displayed here was donated in 1773 to the Church of the Holy Cross Hospital in Miechów by Father Józef Majowicz, a member of the Order of the Holy Sepulchre. The chalice was made by Marcin Lekszycki, a goldsmith in Krakow from 1763 to 1798 and a master of his time. He was one of the few Krakow goldsmiths to sign his work (using the 'ML' guild mark in an oval). Lekszycki ran a large workshop with numerous apprentices; his workshop was located on Bracka Street. He created unique Rococo-style monstrances, ciboria, chalices, sanctuary lamps, censers, incense boats, trays, and candlesticks. Most of the works from Marcin Lekszycki's workshop are housed in churches in Krakow and the former Miechów district. The chalice shown here is made of gilded silver. It is decorated in the Rococo style (shell) and features decorative elements typical of Lekszycki's studio, such as vines, festoons, acanthus leaves, and plant motifs.

two_small_vases.title: 飞鹤花瓶
two_small_vases.description: 这两个小花瓶形状相同：在低矮的凹底上，有一个加长的卵形腹部，双臂演变成相当短而细的颈部，末端是高脚杯状的流嘴。环形底座和流嘴饰有铜制的箍圈装饰，带有镀银痕迹。花瓶装饰有金属掐丝珐琅，使用银丝。装饰描绘了飞翔的仙鹤，白色带有灰色和红色元素，位于深蓝色背景上。仙鹤图案以连续的方式出现在两个花瓶的瓶身上。在流嘴边缘和底座正上方，可以看到一圈圆形的红色图案。在底座下方，可以看到一个类似于日语片假名中的yo音节的符号。These two small vases have the same shape: on a low, concave base, there is an elongated ovoid body, with the arms evolving into a rather short and slender neck, ending in a goblet-shaped spout. The ring base and spout are decorated with copper hoops with traces of silver plating. The vases are decorated with metal cloisonné enamel using silver wire. The decoration depicts flying cranes, white with gray and red elements, on a dark blue background. The crane motif appears continuously on the bodies of both vases. A circular red pattern can be seen around the rim of the spout and just above the base. Below the base, a symbol resembling the 'yo' syllable in Japanese katakana can be seen.

cauldron.title: 釜
cauldron.description: 这口大锅由铜片制成，呈钟形。它由两片金属板构成，分别构成锅底和锅侧。略微凸起的锅底与圆柱形的锅侧连接，采用了罗姆铜匠的传统工艺：开槽并焊接搭接接头。大锅的锅侧顶部略微外扩，壶嘴处形成一个狭窄的平锤式环口。壶嘴边缘下方对称地铆接了两个由弯曲铜棒制成的带有平锤式卷须的凸耳。每个凸耳用三个铜铆钉固定。两个凸耳由一条铁链连接，这条铁链很可能是用来将大锅悬挂在火上的。大锅内部有镀锡的痕迹。涂层因长期使用而磨损。This cauldron is made of copper sheets and is bell-shaped. It is constructed from two metal plates, which form the bottom and the sides of the pot. The slightly convex bottom is connected to the cylindrical sides using a traditional Romani coppersmith technique: grooving and soldering a lap joint. The top of the cauldron's side flares out slightly, forming a narrow, flat-hammered rim at the spout. Below the rim, two lugs made of bent copper rods with flat-hammered tendrils are symmetrically riveted. Each lug is secured with three copper rivets. The two lugs are connected by an iron chain, which was likely used to suspend the cauldron over a fire. The interior of the cauldron shows traces of tinning. The coating is worn from long-term use.

ritual_hare_mask.title: 仪式用野兔面具
ritual_hare_mask.description: 这是马里邦贾加拉悬崖多贡传统面具的典型特征。多贡面具以动物形和几何形体为特色，并配有富有表现力的彩绘装饰，这些装饰通常也以几何图案为主。白色、红色（酒红色、砖红色）和黑色是其主要颜色。大多数面具的面部特征鲜明，呈几何形状（矩形，垂直放置），带有轮廓分明的眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴，或者像所描述的面具一样，面部呈几何形状，呈椭圆形，带有明显的动物形特征。由于其形状，这款面具俗称“野兔面具”。This is a typical feature of traditional Dogon masks from the Bandiagara Escarpment in Mali. Dogon masks are characterized by zoomorphic and geometric forms, accompanied by expressive painted decorations, which are also often dominated by geometric patterns. White, red (burgundy, brick red), and black are its primary colors. Most masks have distinct facial features in geometric shapes (rectangular, placed vertically) with well-defined eyes, nose, and mouth, or, like the mask described, have a geometric, oval-shaped face with pronounced zoomorphic features. Due to its shape, this mask is commonly known as the 'hare mask'.

mikiphone_pocket_phonograph.title: 袖珍留声机
mikiphone_pocket_phonograph.description: 该留声机采用弹簧驱动机构，可播放直径为 10 至 25 厘米、转速为 33 rpm 的唱片。它有时被称为维多利亚时代的随身听和 iPod 的曾祖父。它是最早的袖珍可移动设备之一。“Mikiphone”不需要任何电源，因为它采用弹簧驱动机构和一个带孔盒子形状的小型胶木共鸣器，而不是通常用于扩音的大管。1924 年，日内瓦的匈牙利兄弟 Nicolas 和 Entienne Vadász 以 Vadasz 系统名义为 Mikiphone 的构造申请了专利。不久之后，他们与著名的瑞士 Paillard 公司签订了合同，开始生产袖珍留声机。截至 1927 年，共生产了 180,000 台这种设备，包括带有金色或银色外壳的豪华版。尽管 Mikiphone 是一种移动设备，但要使其工作却并非易事，因为它包含一些小元件，拆卸后可以存放在一个小的金属罐中，因此需要用户非常精确地操作。该设备设计用于以 33 rpm 的转速播放直径为 10 至 25 厘米的唱片。This phonograph uses a spring-driven mechanism and can play records with a diameter of 10 to 25 cm at a speed of 33 rpm. It is sometimes called the Victorian-era Walkman and the great-grandfather of the iPod. It is one of the earliest pocket-sized portable devices. The 'Mikiphone' does not require any power source as it uses a spring-driven mechanism and a small bakelite resonator in the shape of a box with a hole, instead of the large horn typically used for amplification. In 1924, the Hungarian brothers Nicolas and Etienne Vadász of Geneva patented the construction of the Mikiphone under the name Vadasz system. Shortly thereafter, they signed a contract with the famous Swiss company Paillard to begin production of the pocket phonograph. By 1927, 180,000 units of this device had been produced, including luxury versions with gold or silver casings. Although the Mikiphone is a mobile device, getting it to work was not easy, as it contained small components that could be stored in a small metal can after disassembly, requiring very precise operation by the user. The device is designed to play records with a diameter of 10 to 25 cm at a speed of 33 rpm.
